text: Identity and access management policy enforces multi-factor authentication for all privileged accounts. Annual review confirms full compliance with NIST CSF PR.AC-1 requirements. Evidence includes IAM configuration exports and access review logs.

metadata.control_name: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited

text: Physical and logical access to assets is managed through role-based access control. Quarterly access reviews identified three dormant accounts with elevated privileges that were not revoked within the 30-day policy window.

metadata.control_name: Physical access to assets is managed and protected

text: Remote access sessions are authenticated and encrypted via corporate VPN with certificate-based mutual TLS. Split tunneling is disabled enterprise-wide. Compliance verified through network configuration audits.

Continuous monitoring of network traffic for anomalous behavior is operational via Splunk SIEM and Darktrace NDR. Alert thresholds are tuned quarterly. Coverage gap identified for east-west traffic in the development VLAN.

metadata.control_name: The network is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events

text: Physical environment monitoring includes badge access logging, CCTV with 90-day retention, and environmental sensors in server rooms. All datacenters are covered; remote office server closets lack environmental sensors.

metadata.control_name: The physical environment is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events

text: Incident response plan is documented, approved by CISO, and tested via tabletop exercises biannually. Last exercise revealed communication gaps between SOC and legal counsel during data breach scenarios.

metadata.control_name: Response plan is executed during or after an incident

text: Information security policy document covers scope, objectives, and management commitment. Policy was last reviewed and approved by the board in Q4 2025. Distribution confirmed to all employees via policy acknowledgment portal.

Human resource security controls require background checks before employment. Current gap: contractor onboarding process does not consistently enforce background verification for short-term engagements under 30 days.

Asset inventory is maintained in ServiceNow CMDB with automated discovery scans running weekly. Classification labels (public, internal, confidential, restricted) are assigned to 92% of assets. Remaining 8% are legacy systems pending decommission.

Access control policy enforces least privilege and separation of duties. Privileged access management is handled through CyberArk PAM. Quarterly recertification campaigns cover 100% of privileged accounts.

Cryptographic controls policy mandates AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2+ for data in transit. Key management lifecycle is documented. Gap identified: three legacy applications still use TLS 1.0 due to vendor constraints.

Physical security perimeters include mantraps at datacenter entrances, biometric access for server rooms, and 24/7 security guard presence. Compliance fully verified during last physical security audit.

Network security controls include segmentation via next-gen firewalls, IDS/IPS at perimeter and internal chokepoints, and microsegmentation for critical database tier. Change management for firewall rules follows ITIL process.
Supplier relationships security assessment process is documented but not consistently applied. Only tier-1 vendors (12 of 45 total) have undergone formal security assessments in the past 12 months.
Information security incident management process aligns with ISO 27001 A.16.1. Incident classification taxonomy, escalation procedures, and post-incident review processes are documented and tested.
Compliance with legal, statutory, and contractual requirements is reviewed annually. Intellectual property rights and software licensing compliance verified through automated tooling.

metadata.control_name: Compliance with legal and contractual requirements

text: Lawfulness of processing personal data is established through documented legal bases for each processing activity. Consent mechanisms are implemented for marketing communications. Legitimate interest assessments completed for employee monitoring.

Data subject rights fulfillment process handles access, rectification, erasure, and portability requests. Average response time is 18 days against the 30-day requirement. Automated workflow tracks all requests in OneTrust.
Data protection impact assessments are required for high-risk processing activities. Gap: two new AI-driven profiling initiatives launched without completing DPIAs prior to processing commencement.

Breach notification procedures are documented with 72-hour notification timeline to supervisory authority. Internal escalation from SOC to DPO is tested quarterly. Last simulated breach achieved notification within 48 hours.

metadata.control_name: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority

text: Cardholder data environment is segmented from corporate network via dedicated firewall rules. Annual penetration test confirmed no pathways from corporate to CDE. Network diagrams are current and reviewed quarterly.

metadata.control_name: Install and maintain network security controls

text: Default passwords and security parameters are changed on all system components before deployment. Partial gap: two point-of-sale terminals in a satellite office retained vendor default SNMP community strings.

metadata.control_name: Apply secure configurations to all system components

text: Stored cardholder data is protected with AES-256 encryption and tokenization for primary account numbers. Encryption key rotation occurs annually. No full PAN is stored in application logs verified by automated scanning.

Audit logging is enabled on all CDE systems capturing authentication events, access to cardholder data, and administrative actions. Log integrity is ensured via write-once storage. Centralized in Splunk with 12-month retention.

metadata.control_name: Log and monitor all access to system components and cardholder data

text: Logical access controls restrict information and systems to authorized users. User access reviews performed quarterly for in-scope SOC 2 systems. One exception noted: a shared service account for legacy ETL process lacks individual accountability.

System operations monitoring includes uptime dashboards, automated alerting for performance degradation, and monthly capacity planning reviews. Change management follows documented SDLC with peer review and approval gates.

Risk assessment process identifies and evaluates threats to achieving service commitments. Annual risk assessment completed with executive sponsorship. Risk register maintained in GRC platform with quarterly updates.

Technical safeguards for electronic protected health information include access controls, audit controls, integrity controls, and transmission security. Gap: automatic logoff is not enforced on clinical workstations in two satellite clinics.

Administrative safeguards include workforce training, security management process, and information access management. Annual HIPAA security awareness training completion rate is 97%. Three new hires pending completion within grace period.

Physical safeguards for ePHI include facility access controls, workstation use policies, and device and media controls. Gap: disposal procedures for portable media containing ePHI are documented but not auditable due to lack of destruction certificates from the third-party vendor.

Right to erasure (right to be forgotten) procedures are implemented with automated data discovery and deletion workflows. Personal data can be erased from primary systems within 7 days of validated request. Gap: erasure from backup systems relies on natural expiry of 30-day retention cycle rather than active removal.

metadata.control_name: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)

text: Data protection by design and by default is implemented through mandatory privacy reviews in the SDLC. New applications undergo privacy architecture review before development. Gap: two legacy applications predating the policy have not been retrofitted with privacy-by-design controls including data minimization and purpose limitation enforcement.

metadata.control_name: Data protection by design and by default

text: Secure development lifecycle processes mandate code reviews, static application security testing, and vulnerability remediation before production deployment. Gap: SAST tooling coverage reaches only 78% of repositories; 22% of internal tools and scripts lack automated security scanning.

metadata.control_name: Develop and maintain secure systems and software

text: Access to cardholder data and CDE system components is restricted based on business need-to-know. Role-based access control matrix is documented and reviewed quarterly. All access grants require manager approval with documented justification stored in the IAM ticketing system.

metadata.control_name: Restrict access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know

text: Strong authentication mechanisms are enforced for all CDE access. Multi-factor authentication is required for all administrative access and all remote access to the CDE. Gap: one legacy payment terminal management interface supports only single-factor authentication pending vendor firmware update.

metadata.control_name: Identify users and authenticate access to system components

text: Operations security procedures including change management, capacity management, and separation of development/test/production environments are documented and enforced. Gap: three development teams have read-only access to production logs that should be restricted to the SRE team only.

Protection from malware is implemented through EDR on all endpoints, email gateway sandboxing, and web proxy with content inspection. Malware signature updates are deployed within 4 hours of vendor release. All controls verified operational through quarterly testing.

Backup policy and procedures comply with A.12.3 requirements. Daily incremental and weekly full backups are performed for all classified systems. Restoration tests are conducted quarterly. Gap: backup encryption key escrow procedures are documented but have not been tested in a key recovery scenario.

Security requirements for information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance are defined in the secure SDLC policy. Threat modeling is required for new systems handling Confidential or Restricted data. Gap: third-party COTS software procurement does not consistently include security requirements in RFP evaluation criteria.

Security in development and support processes includes secure coding standards, SAST/DAST integration in CI/CD, and mandatory peer review for all code changes. Test environments are separated from production with sanitized data. Compliance verified through pipeline audit logs and code review metrics.

metadata.control_name: Security in development and support processes

text: California Consumer Privacy Act compliance program includes consumer rights management for access, deletion, and opt-out of sale requests. Privacy notice is published and updated annually. Gap: the do-not-sell mechanism does not cover all data sharing arrangements with analytics partners classified as sales under CCPA/CPRA regulations.

metadata.control_name: Consumer right to know about personal information collected

text: Consumer right to deletion is implemented with automated workflows triggered through the privacy portal. Deletion requests are fulfilled within 45 days as required. Service provider contracts include deletion obligations. Gap: three legacy data warehouses require manual deletion intervention that occasionally exceeds the 45-day timeline.

metadata.control_name: Consumer right to deletion of personal information

text: Consumer right to opt-out of sale or sharing of personal information is implemented via Global Privacy Control signal recognition and a prominent opt-out link on the website. Opt-out preferences are propagated to all downstream data processors within 15 business days.

metadata.control_name: Consumer right to opt-out of sale or sharing

text: GDPR records of processing activities are maintained for all data processing operations involving EU resident personal data. The processing register includes purpose, legal basis, data categories, retention periods, and technical measures. Register is reviewed quarterly by the DPO and updated within 5 business days of any processing change.

Data protection officer is appointed and registered with the supervisory authority. DPO has direct reporting line to the board, is involved in all data protection matters, and conducts annual compliance audits. DPO independence is maintained with no conflicts of interest in other organizational roles.

metadata.control_name: Designation, position, and tasks of the data protection officer

text: PCI DSS vulnerability management program requires internal and external vulnerability scans on a quarterly basis. ASV scans are conducted by an approved scanning vendor. Gap: remediation of medium-severity findings identified in the last external ASV scan exceeded the 90-day remediation window for 4 of 12 findings.

metadata.control_name: Test security of systems and networks regularly

text: Information security policy for all personnel is maintained and enforced per PCI DSS Requirement 12. Annual security awareness training covers PCI-specific requirements. Incident response plan includes PCI-specific procedures for cardholder data breach. Gap: acceptable use policy does not explicitly address PCI DSS scope for all personnel with CDE access.

metadata.control_name: Support information security with organizational policies and programs

text: Operations security logging and monitoring controls per A.12.4 are implemented with centralized log collection in the SIEM platform. Administrator and operator activities are logged with immutable audit trails. Clock synchronization via NTP ensures log correlation accuracy. Gap: log review for 5 non-critical systems is performed monthly rather than the required weekly cadence.

CCPA non-discrimination requirement is met with no price or service differences for consumers who exercise their privacy rights. Loyalty program participation is available regardless of opt-out status. Financial incentive programs for data collection include required notice and opt-in consent mechanisms.

Test data management in development environments complies with A.14.3 requirements. Production data used in testing is anonymized through approved masking procedures. Gap: one QA environment was identified with a 6-month-old copy of production data that had not been refreshed with anonymized data as required by policy. Remediation initiated immediately upon discovery.
